output.brief: The jump in DC-stage write-offs is most likely caused by our own night receiving, not by Haverlow. The night team was cut from six to four on 27 July. Since then, median time from unloading to chamber has gone from 44 minutes to nearly 4 hours. Pallets sit on an unrefrigerated dock at 15–17°C. Night-shift write-off rates rose from 0.6% to 2.9% across all suppliers, while day shift stayed flat. Haverlow's trailer data shows product at 2.4–3.5°C when doors opened, with no alarms. The "warm" receipt probe readings are taken at confirmation, after the dock delay, so they measure our delay and not Haverlow's product. The chambers held temperature. Do not raise the chargeback or move volume: it would penalise the wrong party and leave the cause in place. Do not drop the night probe, which would hide the problem. Restore night staffing, or otherwise cut dock-to-chamber time, set a maximum time, and monitor it weekly from scan data. Separately, the Corriebank credit rise (from 3 August, self-certified claims) is unproven. Pull a sample of claims and match them to lots and receiving shift before changing terms. I am fairly confident in the main finding. I am less sure how much of the credit rise is over-claiming.
